title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: Sales Development agent books seller meetings for prospects
summary: The roadmap description, activation and blocking controls, and preview consumption billing are supported. Minor corrections are needed to cite the source for blocking all instances and align the checklist's individual-instance blocking advice with the controls table.

Public Preview availability^3^ | November 24, 2026 | December 1, 2026 | December 1, 2026 |

claims.claim: The account and persistent Microsoft 365 resources cost 100 Copilot Credits per agent per month.
claims.quote: The agent account, email address, and persistent access to Microsoft 365 resources (for example, Exchange and OneDrive workspaces) have a recurring charge of 100 Copilot Credits per agent per month.

claims.claim: Agent activity incurs additional consumption billing.
claims.quote: All agent activity is billed consumptively.

claims.claim: The Sales Development Agent's accountable user must have consumption billing enabled.
claims.quote: Sales Development Agent and Service Agent: The person responsible for the agent (that is, the accountable user to whom the agent is assigned) is required to have consumption billing enabled.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Blocking a template agent turns off all instances created under it.
claims.quote: Blocking an agent automatically turns off all instances created under that agent. These instances remain inactive until the IT admin unblocks the agent.
claims.fix: Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365/admin/manage-agents#actions-for-agent-365-agents for the all-instances statement; the current agent-actions citation does not contain that statement, but the Learn search excerpt for manage-agents does.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Administrators can block an individual agent instance to stop it.
claims.quote: Blocking an instance stops it and any actions it's performing.

claims.claim: Individual-instance blocking is documented in the Microsoft 365 admin center's Agents > All Agents area.
claims.quote:
In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Agents > All Agents.
Select an agent from the list. A panel opens.
Under the Details tab, select the Instances tab to see all instances created by that agent.
Select an instance and choose Block.

claims.claim: The Package Management API lists block, unblock and reassign operations.
claims.quote: Block, unblock, and reassign ownership of packages.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The checklist's instruction to block an individual instance has a corresponding controls-table row.
claims.quote: Checklist: "Block the agent or an instance". Table rows cover activation, organisation-wide blocking, and a scheduling-only switch; no row covers individual-instance blocking.
claims.fix: In the After rollout checklist, replace 'Block the agent or an instance if booked meetings show wrong or unauthorised behaviour' with 'Block the agent if booked meetings show wrong or unauthorised behaviour'.
